subject: Break-glass: temporary fair-share token uplift / SLA elevation request (Bridge Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@bridge-thera.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bridge-thera.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@bridge-thera.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term fair-share uplift for product launch week

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We’re greenlit for a controlled launch of our clinical triage pilot on 26 July, and early traffic projections show a concentrated burst pattern during the first 72 hours that exceeds our current token allocation per minute under the standard fair-share policy.

Attached is a usage snapshot and the product launch week plan. We need a temporary uplift to our fair-share token pool (token-per-minute soft limit) for the window 26–28 July. Key asks:
- A short-term uplift to the fair-share bucket to reduce throttling for our background inference (mainly embeddings + chat routing).
- A documented SLA note that during the uplift window Redwood will avoid preemptive throttling for our production route unless total cluster capacity is exhausted.

We understand this is an exception; happy to take a carveout that includes an elevated price and an agreed rollback time. Can you confirm feasibility and what information you need from procurement?

Jordan
Head of Product, Bridge Therapeutics
(614) 555-0198

Attachments: bridge-proposed-multipass-SLA.pdf (pdf), fairshare-usage-snapshot-2026-07-14.csv (csv)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@bridge-thera.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term fair-share uplift for product launch week

Jordan —

Appreciate the heads up and the data. Short answer: we can do a time-boxed fair-share uplift, but we need internal alignment on operational guardrails and an acceptance of a reduced latency SLO in extreme saturation scenarios.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) I’ll open an internal exception request and tag infra on the exact resource window you want (please confirm your peak hours in UTC).
2) Procurement: we typically formalize with an addendum that describes the uplift window, uplift multiplier, price delta, and rollback triggers.
3) Ops contingency: we’ll require a pre-launch runbook and a contact list for the on-call engineer during the window.

Can you confirm: expected peak window in UTC, estimated request rate per minute, and whether critical flows can tolerate a 200–300 ms median latency bump if we hit system-wide contention? If you can provide that by EOD tomorrow we’ll fast-track an operational carveout.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Break-glass: temporary fair-share token uplift / SLA elevation request

Avery —

Looping infra & product ops. Short internal summary: Bridge wants a 72-hour elevated fair-share (tokens/min) for a launch. They’ve offered to accept an addendum and higher rates. Risks:
- If we grant an uplift without capacity reservation, we rely on fair-share preemption logic — elevated tokens could reduce availability for other tenants unless we put a soft cap on the uplift and include fallback model variants.
- Latency: we can promise a relaxed SLO (e.g., 95th percentile +200ms) but only if we enable burst throttling thresholds and a temporary priority token pool.

Proposed internal carveout (for approval):
- Window: 2026-07-26T00:00:00Z to 2026-07-28T23:59:59Z
- Uplift: 3x current fair-share tokens/min (subject to absolute cluster ceiling of X tokens/min)
- Priority pool: allocate ephemeral tokens drawn from a priority pool that expires at window end; if cluster utilization > 85%, automatic model-variant fallback and 429 responses for non-critical background jobs.
- Price: +45% for uplift window (to be added to contract addendum)
- Rollback & monitoring: 1-min granularity metrics; runbook required; ops on-call to be scheduled (assign: Monica)

Irene — can you confirm feasibility of implementing an ephemeral priority pool and a circuit-breaker that flips at 85% cluster utilization? If yes, we’ll prep the addendum and notify sales/legal for an expedited approval.

Rishi
Principal Product Manager, Platform

Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Break-glass: temporary fair-share token uplift / SLA elevation request

Folks —

We can implement a temporary priority token pool and a utilization circuit-breaker with the following constraints:
- Implementation ETA: 48 hours for config changes in the routing/orchestration layer + 12 hours to smoke-test on staging under representative load.
- Circuit-breaker threshold: configurable; 85% recommended. When triggered:
  - non-critical background jobs receive 429s
  - critical production routes reroute to model-variant with slightly lower compute (quantized variant) to preserve throughput
- Enforcement: priority pool will be billed separately and tied to the addendum; tokens are ephemeral and will zero out at window end.

Operational ask for Bridge: provide their peak-hour UTC window and a short runbook for what they consider "non-critical" traffic. We also need a named on-call for the window.

I’ll prepare a short implementation checklist and hand to Monica to coordinate the runbook and the addendum pricing details. Once Monica confirms, Avery — you can share the formal carveout offer with Bridge.

Irene
Director, Platform Reliability

Subject: Final: temporary fair-share uplift — approved with conditions (BRG-4821)

Jordan / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turn. Internal ops has approved a time-boxed uplift under the following conditions (summary below; full addendum to follow from Legal):

Summary of approved carveout (concise):
- Window: 2026-07-26T00:00:00Z through 2026-07-28T23:59:59Z
- Uplift: 3x fair-share tokens/min, enforced via an ephemeral priority token pool (tokens will be charged separately at +45% uplift rate).
- Circuit-breaker: will engage at 85% cluster utilization. On trigger: non-critical background jobs will receive rate-limit 429s; critical routes will be served by a quantized model-variant to preserve throughput.
- Latency SLO: median expected latency may increase by up to 200–300 ms at 95th percentile during the uplift window; Redwood will not issue SLA credits for latency increases caused by cluster-wide saturation during that window.
- Rollback & monitoring: 1-min resolution dashboards will be shared; Redwood will run a pre-launch smoke test on 2026-07-24 (please confirm a 2-hour window).
- On-call: Bridge must provide a named on-call engineer reachable by Slack + cell for the uplift window (send name by EOD Monday).

Next steps:
1) Procurement: expect an addendum draft from Redwood Legal by Mon 2026-07-20.
2) Bridge: confirm peak-hour UTC and provide the on-call & runbook.
3) Ops: Monica will schedule smoke test and runbook rehearsal.

Apologies for the compressed timeline; we’ll do our best to make the rollout smooth.

—Avery
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
